Hallem2006.extracted_from: DoOR.data per-receptor CSVs, column Hallem.2006.EN (24 Ors, empty-neuron ab3A expression, 10^-2 in paraffin oil; 110 odours + SFR row). Values are net spikes/s (spontaneous subtracted; negative = inhibition); SFR row = spontaneous spikes/s.

caveats: door_response is DoOR consensus, normalised 0-1 per responding unit across odours (max response of that unit = 1); NOT Hz and not comparable in absolute magnitude across receptors. The DoOR matrix is NOT SFR-subtracted: an SFR row exists and DoOR::reset_sfr() subtracts it; door_response_minus_sfr = door_response - SFR row value (can be negative = inhibition).
Hallem & Carlson 2006 did NOT test 3-octanol or 4-methylcyclohexanol (absent from the 110-odour Hallem.2006.EN set); hallem_delta_hz is null for OCT/MCH. Benzaldehyde is present for all 24 Ors.
Hallem et al. 2004 (empty-neuron) has 3-octanol values for only a few Ors (hallem2004_delta_hz); MCH absent.
The DoOR solvent row is the solvent/mineral-oil control; there is no pure-air row. Using SFR (spontaneous) as the air baseline is a modelling choice.

Glomerulus null = receptor not expressed in adult antenna/palp or not mapped in DoOR (e.g. larval Ors Or85c, Or45b, Or30a, Or1a, Or22c, Or24a, Or45a, Or59a, Or74a, Or94a/b). Some units are sensillum-level summed recordings (ac1, ac2, ac4, ac3_noOr35a, pb2A, ab2B, ab3B, ab4B, ab5B) mapping to multiple glomeruli (e.g. "VL1+VM1+VL2p"); split or drop them when mapping to single ORN_<glom> types. Duplicate units map to the same glomerulus (e.g. Or85a & ab2B -> DM5; Or47a & ab5B -> DM3; Or33a & ab4B -> DA2; Or85b & ab3B -> VM5d; Or35a & ac3B -> VC3; Or33c/Or85e/pb2A -> VC1; Or49a & Or85f -> DL4; Or22a & Or22b -> DM2). Or33b is co-expressed in two classes (DM5+DM3).

DoOR glomerulus names: Or69a -> "D" (current nomenclature D), Gr21a.Gr63a -> "V", ac3A -> "DL2d/v" ambiguous, Or42a -> VM7d, Or59c -> VM7v, Or46a -> VA7l; check hemibrain/FlyWire naming (e.g. VM7d vs "VM7", VC3 vs VC3l/VC3m, VM5d/VM5v, VA1d/VA1v) when joining to ORN_<glom> cell types.
Mapping taken verbatim from DoOR.data door_mappings.csv; nothing here was invented. OCT used by DoOR is racemic 3-octanol (CAS 589-98-0); MCH is mixed cis/trans (CAS 589-91-3).

DoOR consensus for OCT/MCH rests on relatively few datasets (MCH: 26 units with data; OCT: 48), mostly de Bruyne 1999/2001, Kreher 2005/2008, Silbering 2011, Münch 2016 GC-imaging; values at mixed concentrations.

hallem2004_delta_hz values are copied as stored in DoOR.data (Hallem.2004.EN, spikes/s); whether they are spontaneous-subtracted and at which dilution was not independently checked against the paper (unverified). Their solvent-row values look like raw rates rather than deltas, so treat them with caution.
